race_context: West Central School Corporation is based in Francesville and runs two schools on US 421: West Central Elementary School and West Central Middle/High School. The superintendent is Dr. Cathy Rowe {wc_home}. The ballot office names for its board seats list Pulaski and Jasper counties {in_list}.

Enrollment: in October 2025 Superintendent Rowe said average daily membership would be about 609.66 students, 11.75 below budget. She put the Education Fund loss at about $88,000 and said about 77 tuition transfers come into the district {wc_m251002}. In October 2026 she said membership would come in around 583.71 rather than the forecast 605, a funding loss of more than $160,000 for the next calendar year {wc_m261001}.

The board has seven members. The district lists them by area: Jonathan Gutwein (Gilliam Township, president), Darin Gudeman (White Post Township, vice president), Jake Tanner (Jefferson Township, secretary), Jeff Lowry (Beaver Township), Todd Miller (Salem Township), Heather Reese (Cass Township) and Dennis Gutwein (at large) {wc_board}{wc_m260108}.

Cass Township seat: Kyle McTeigue won it unopposed in 2022 {pp_2022}. On Nov. 6, 2025 the board voted 6-0 to appoint Heather Reese to the seat McTeigue left vacant {wc_m251106}. Reese is the only 2026 candidate {in_list}{pp_ballot}.

Salem Township seat: in 2022 Todd Miller won reelection over Lindsey Geyer, 467 votes to 387 {pp_2022}. The district lists Miller's term as ending in 2026 {wc_board}. He is not on the 2026 ballot, so the seat is open. The candidates are Lindsey Geyer and Jamie (Jay) Johnson, both listed as Republicans {in_list}{pp_ballot}.

The district site also lists a 2026 term end for Jeff Lowry's Beaver Township seat, which he won unopposed in 2022. Neither the state list nor the Pulaski Post's ballot list shows a Beaver Township race in 2026 {wc_board}{pp_2022}{in_list}{pp_ballot}.

Budget: the board adopted the 2026 budget, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan 6-0 in October 2025 {wc_m251002}. On Oct. 1, 2026 it adopted the 2027 budget and plans 6-0. At the same meeting it approved a transfer from the Education Fund to the Operations Fund and a transfer to the Rainy Day Fund {wc_m261001}. In September 2026 Superintendent Rowe raised a concern about the effect on the Education Fund of a large graduating class against a small incoming kindergarten class {wc_m260903}. The minutes reviewed do not discuss the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) or a referendum.

Staffing: in May 2026 the board approved 6-0 a reduction in force to a partial contract, and in June 2026 a reduction in force in high school music {wc_m260507}{wc_m260604}. In April 2026 it approved Teacher Appreciation Grant distributions 5-1, with Jeff Lowry voting no {wc_m260402}.

Facilities: a renovation project was wrapping up in January 2026 {wc_m260108}. A Feb. 19, 2026 hail storm damaged the middle/high school roof and outbuildings. Rowe said in October 2026 that the claim came to $2,137,013 and that insurance paid it less a $100,000 deductible {wc_m260507}{wc_m261001}. She said in August 2026 that the wind/hail deductible will rise to $250,000 at renewal {wc_m260806}.

Wind turbine costs: in September 2025 a transfer from the Rainy Day Fund to the Wind Turbine Maintenance Fund failed 1-6 {wc_m250904}. In February 2026 the board approved a Turbine Maintenance Fund resolution 6-1, with Jeff Lowry voting no {wc_m260205}. Rowe later met with other districts that own turbines about common concerns {wc_m260604}.

Academics: Rowe reported in April 2026 that 60% of West Central students passed IREAD, against 49% statewide {wc_m260402}. In May 2026 the middle/high school principal said the school had not earned Early College endorsement {wc_m260507}. In February 2026 he said that beginning in 2026-27, students scoring above proficiency on ILEARN with at least a C in math would be auto-enrolled in advanced math {wc_m260205}.

Policies: in August 2026 the board adopted a wireless devices prohibition policy (4307) 4-0 {wc_m260806}. Sunday use of school facilities came up twice. In January 2026 the board rejected Sunday volleyball league practices 4-3, with Todd Miller, Dennis Gutwein, Jake Tanner and Heather Reese voting no. In February 2026 it approved them 6-1 with a 1 p.m. earliest start, with Miller voting no {wc_m260108}{wc_m260205}.
No candidate forum, questionnaire or news profile for the 2026 West Central races was found.
